harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 (OPNsense) as router between lan-a (vtnet1/opt1, 10.60.10.0/24, toward node2) and lan-b (vtnet2/opt2, 10.60.20.0/24, toward node3). Added a logged pf block rule for TCP/23 on both opt1 and opt2 (other traffic still passes), verified a telnet-style attempt from node2 to node3 is refused and logged on node1's filter log, then restarted all three nodes one at a time and re-verified the block+log behavior and network state persisted after each restart.
actions_performed: Discovered actual topology: node1 (OPNsense/FreeBSD) has vtnet0 (shared mgmt network), vtnet1 (link to node2), vtnet2 (link to node3); node2/node3 (Ubuntu 16.04) each have ens2 (mgmt) and ens7 (lan link)
Assigned OPNsense interfaces opt1=lan-a (10.60.10.1/24 on vtnet1) and opt2=lan-b (10.60.20.1/24 on vtnet2) via config.xml edit + configctl interface reconfigure

Added pf filter rules per interface: block+log TCP port 23 (quick), then pass-all for other traffic; applied via configctl filter reload; fixed a duplicate-port XML bug found via the PHP filter-compile error
Statically configured node2 ens7=10.60.10.2/24 and node3 ens7=10.60.20.2/24 persistently via /etc/network/interfaces.d/*.cfg, with cross-LAN static routes added the same way
Verified cross-LAN ping works (pass rule) and a TCP/23 connection from node2 to node3 times out (blocked)
Located and displayed the OPNsense filter log entry on node1 (/var/log/filter/filter_20260905.log) showing block,in on vtnet1 from 10.60.10.2 (node2) to 10.60.20.2 port 23
Captured pre-restart boot markers (FreeBSD kern.boottime; Linux /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id) and health evidence for all 3 nodes
Restarted node1, node2, node3 sequentially (one at a time) using native reboot (shutdown -r now), polled each until exec was available again, and confirmed each node's boot marker changed

Post-restart, re-verified on all nodes: interface IPs/routes persisted, pf rules present, forwarding enabled, cross-LAN ping still works, and a repeat telnet attempt from node2 to node3:23 was again blocked and logged on node1
Cleaned up temporary nc listener on node3 and scratch files on node1

evidence.requirement: node1 routes between lan-a and lan-b
evidence.summary: node1's vtnet1/vtnet2 identified as links to node2/node3 respectively; configured as opt1=lan-a/opt2=lan-b; cross-LAN ping from node2 (10.60.10.2) to node3 (10.60.20.2) succeeds through node1.

evidence.requirement: Refuse TCP port 23 between lan-a and lan-b
evidence.summary: pf ruleset shows block-quick-log rules for tcp port 23 on vtnet1 and vtnet2; live telnet-style (nc) connection attempts from node2 to node3:23 time out both before and after restart.

evidence.requirement: Record every refused attempt in a log on node1
evidence.summary: node1's /var/log/filter/filter_20260905.log contains block,in entries on vtnet1 tagged with the block rule's label, for every SYN retry from 10.60.10.2 to 10.60.20.2:23, both pre- and post-restart.

evidence.requirement: Show a log entry produced by an attempt made from node2
evidence.summary: Filter log line: block,in on vtnet1 from 10.60.10.2 (node2) to 10.60.20.2 port 23 -- directly attributable to node2's nc connection attempt.
Baseline kern.boottime captured (1788629867); reboot acknowledged; exec available again; new kern.boottime (1788630221) proves restart; interfaces, pf rules, and forwarding all recovered.

Baseline boot_id (dbb46974...) captured with working ens7/route; reboot acknowledged (connection closed); exec available again; new boot_id (0cc1a8be...) proves restart; ens7 config, route, and cross-LAN ping all recovered.

Baseline boot_id (2dffe735...) captured with working ens7/route; reboot acknowledged (connection closed); exec available again; new boot_id (7368881f...) proves restart; ens7 config, route, and cross-LAN ping all recovered.

After all three nodes were restarted, a fresh telnet attempt from node2 to node3:23 was blocked and a new matching log entry appeared on node1, confirming the policy survives node restarts; listener cleaned up afterward.
